html:
For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y(a)=c, the increment in y using the Runge-Kutta Method with step size Δx is computed as the weighted average of four sample slopes: Δy=16(y′+2y1′+2y2′+y3′)⋅Δx, where

  • y′=f(x,y) is the slope at the initial point (x,y),

  • y1′=f(x1,y1) is the slope at (x1,y1)=(x+12Δx,y+12y′⋅Δx),

  • y2′=f(x2,y2) is the slope at (x2,y2)=(x+12Δx,y+12y1′⋅Δx),

  • y3′=f(x3,y3) is the slope at (x3,y3)=(x+Δx,y+y2′⋅Δx).

Since we want to find the value of y at x=1, we will use a step size of Δx=1−0=1.

First, we create a table and add the initial condition data.

x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
0 1

Now let's find the required values.

  • First, we compute the value of y′ according to the given rule: y′=3x(y−2)=3(0)(1−2)=0. So, we add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    0 1 0

  • The first intermediate point is (x1,y1)=(x+12Δx,y+12y′⋅Δx)=(0+12⋅1,1+12⋅0⋅1)=(12,1). So, the first intermediate slope is y1′=3x1(y1−2)=3⋅12⋅(1−2)=−32. We can add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    0 1 0 −32

  • The second intermediate point is (x2,y2)=(x+12Δx,y+12y1′⋅Δx)=(0+12⋅1,1+12⋅(−32)⋅1)=(12,14). So, the second intermediate slope is y2′=3x2(y2−2)=3⋅12⋅(14−2)=−218. We add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    0 1 0 −32 −218

  • The third intermediate point is (x3,y3)=(x+Δx,y+y2′⋅Δx)=(0+1,1+(−218)⋅1)=(1,−138). So, the third intermediate slope is y3′=3x3(y3−2)=3(1)(−138−2)=−878. We can add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    0 1 0 −32 −218 −878

  • Finally, we compute Δy using the Runge-Kutta Method: Δy=16(y′+2y1′+2y2′+y3′)⋅Δx=16(0+2⋅(−32)+2⋅(−218)+(−878))⋅1=16(−248−428−878)=16⋅(−1538)=−5116. We add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    0 1 0 −32 −218 −878 −5116

To get the values of x and y in the next row, we add Δx to x and Δy to y, as follows:

xnew=x+Δx=0+1=1ynew=y+Δy=1+(−5116)=−3516

Adding these rows to our table gives the following:

x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
0 1 0 −32 −218 −878 −5116
1 −3516

Therefore, we conclude that y(1)≈−3516.
